issues.description: The algorithm is correct in intent but is implemented as a global fixed-point iteration that repeatedly scans all M train information records until no changes. In the worst case this can require O(N * M) work (dp values can propagate across stations many times), which is not acceptable for the problem constraints (N, M up to 2e5). This will lead to timeouts on large test cases and therefore the solution will fail on performance grounds.

No tests or test harness were provided with the submission. There are no unit tests or integration tests to verify correctness on representative inputs or to catch regressions (include at least unit tests covering sample cases and one large-case performance test).

The solution relies on a global while-changed loop with full scans of train_info (procedural, tightly coupled iteration). This design mixes the relaxation/control logic and the iteration strategy; it would be better to separate concerns and use a data structure (priority queue / Dijkstra-like approach) that avoids repeated full scans.

The code uses float('inf') as a sentinel for "any time" (dp[N] = float('inf')). Although handled explicitly, mixing float sentinel values with integer arithmetic is fragile and requires special-case branches. Prefer an integer sentinel or an explicit flag for "unbounded" to avoid subtle issues.
Linter warnings: ambiguous variable name 'l' (lowercase L) is used for departure time; consider using a clearer name (e.g., start or l0) to avoid confusion and linter warnings.
